articles.title: Game, set … match? Can a dating coach help you win at love?
articles.summary: Would you pay thousands to meet the love of your life? In an age of app fatigue, many singles are hiring coaches to help them find partners. But are they chancers preying on the lovelorn, or do they hold the key to true romance? Modern dating is a hellscape.
body: Modern dating is a hellscape. Just ask any single person, who will probably regale you with stories of endless swiping, ghosting, cringe Hinge dates and unfulfilling “situationships”. But what if there was a way to escape all this and put yourself on a fast track to finding The One?

How did the coaching actually work? Yarrow’s programme was based around identifying Izzy’s “limiting beliefs” about herself – for example, that she was “going to be single for ever” – and challenging the ways they were holding her back from finding love. The first step was delving into her romantic past, all the way back to her first kiss, to find the origin of her insecurities. “Through that, so many things surfaced – some of the terrible, awful horror stories I hadn’t really shared or picked up on, even from being a teenager,” Izzy remembers. “Obviously, that shapes who we are now. So we did a full retrospective.”

articles.title: Steal My Food Itinerary: 3 Days in Sifnos, Greece
articles.summary: It felt like everyone I know traveled to Greece this summer. Friends chose Zakynthos, Crete, Naxos, Ikaria. I opted for Sifnos, one of the Cyclades’ most celebrated food destinations but still, thankfully, relatively under the radar internationally.
body: Just 3 hours from Athens by ferry, this Cycladic island is best experienced around the table.

Our trip landed in the middle of August — peak tourist season in the Mediterranean — but it never felt cramped. And now that summer has come to a close, what crowds there were have thinned and temperatures are more forgiving, yet peak-season produce is still finding its way into dishes across the island. So now is an even better time to experience Sifnos.

Getting there means starting in Athens, where ferries come in and out of the port of Piraeus from all across the Aegean and Ionian seas. The 2.5-hour trip from Athens to Sifnos is a thrill — worthy of a few Dramamine tablets if you’re prone to seasickness — with incredible views of the islands you pass along the way. The Aegean really is a different shade of blue; it’s tempting to gaze into it from the deck the whole way.

articles.title: I Tried Snap Specs, and They Could Be the Future of Smart Glasses
articles.summary: Snap was in the smart glasses game from the jump. The company’s original camera-equipped Spectacles debuted back in 2016, beating Meta to the market by five years. Meta’s Ray-Bans and Oakleys captured massive consumer mindshare anyway, while Snap’s smart eyewear has been less visible.
body: With Snap Specs, though, the company is aiming to make up for lost time by delivering smart glasses that go beyond a hidden camera and voice-activated AI. At the Snapdragon 2026 Summit, I got my hands (and eyes) on a pair of Snap’s soon-to-be-released spatial-computing glasses that overlay digital graphics onto the physical world.

The in-glasses display is surprisingly bright. Specs' visuals are powered by a proprietary liquid crystal on silicon (LCoS) display system, and even when used in a light-filled conference room, I could still clearly see the UI and its various apps. I tested out YouTube under these borderline abusive conditions, and it streamed high-def video in 16 million colors suitably.

The display offers a 51-degree field of view. It feels like having a large floating window hovering in front of you. From there, you can use simple gestures to launch apps, watch movies, play games, and do most other tasks you can’t do from your phone. But it was the context-aware, real-world spatial computing tasks that I wanted to try—the things you can't do from a phone or PC.
points: Snap was in the smart glasses game from the jump.

articles.title: An Essential Guide to the Amalfi Coast—Italy’s Definition of Dolce Vita Glam
articles.summary: The seaside stretch skirting the Sorrentine Peninsula rose to international fame in the 1950s and ‘60s, but the cliffside paradise claims a rich history dating back to the Middle Ages.
body: Monasterio Santa Rosa'd 20 antique-accented rooms have taken over from original dwellings for nuns.

Running along the tip of the Sorrentine Peninsula, from Vietri sul Mare in the east to Positano, the Amalfi Drive strings together a majority of the coastline’s 13 towns. While the drive is dubbed one of the world’s most scenic, if you’re not familiar with Italy’s narrow mountain roads (or drivers, for that matter), skip renting a car and explore the region by ferry, taxi, or the main bus line, SITA SUD, instead. Another option? The Path of the Gods hike, a 4.3-mile former shepherd’s trail that ends just above Positano—and you can descend down 1,700 timeworn stone steps to the seaside town below.

articles.title: BA's Best Masala Chai
articles.summary: This chai is definitively ginger-forward. Feel free to add a little more maple syrup if you like it on the sweeter side. This is part of BA’s Best, a collection of our essential recipes.
body: This masala chai is unapologetically gingery, warmly spiced with cinnamon and cardamom, and just sweet enough from maple syrup. The ginger and cinnamon simmer until intensely fragrant before strong black tea joins the pot; Assam is ideal, though sturdy tea bags like PG Tips work too.

Former food director Carla Lalli Music adapted the recipe from a chai she fell for at her former yoga studio. Her friend Spiros Antonopoulos, who made the tea there, had learned the method from a chai wallah (a tea maker and vendor) he knew in Taos, New Mexico; Carla eventually persuaded Spiros to share it and translated his instinctive recipe into precise measurements. His method brought the milky tea nearly to a boil three times for a deeper, caramelized flavor. This version streamlines that technique: Let the chai foam up once, then pull it from the heat and give it a five-minute rest before straining.

Masala chai, which translates to “spiced tea,” is black tea brewed with milk and aromatic spices. There’s no single formula; this version keeps the spice mix relatively streamlined, leaning heavily on fresh ginger with cinnamon and green cardamom.
points: Feel free to add a little more maple syrup if you like it on the sweeter side.
